President
window: Dr. Lizette Navarette is a passionate student-centered leader with two decades of experience in higher education and local government. Dr. Navarette was appointed as President of Woodland Community College (WCC) in December 2023.

Prior to joining Woodland Community College, Dr. Navarette served as Executive Vice Chancellor at the California Community College Chancellor’s Office where she led the Office of Institutional Supports and Success which included college finance, facilities, institutional effectiveness, and government relations. She was responsible for formulating policies that determine the distribution of over $13 billion in local assistance and capital outlay funds to the state’s 73 community college districts, professional development which advances student success, and coordinating state and federal matters for the system. From October 2022 to June 2023, Dr. Navarette served as Interim Deputy Chancellor of the California Community Colleges. She previously served as the Vice Chancellor of College Finance and Facilities Planning and was the first woman to hold that position. Navarette has also served as the Vice President of the Community College League of California, Associate Director of Regional Relations for the University of California Riverside, and as the Youth & Education Coordinator for the City of Riverside.

Dr. Navarette has an extensive history championing student success, affordability, and equitable educational opportunities for all students. She earned a bachelor’s degree in political science and international relations from UC Riverside, a master’s degree in public administration from the University of La Verne, and a doctorate in education from UC Davis. In 2021, Dr. Navarette earned the United Nations Global Education for All award for her research on working adult learners. Navarette is a proud first-generation graduate. She serves on the California Community Colleges Chief Executive Officers Board and the Community College Facilities Coalition Board.

Kathy Sorensen brings nearly three decades of dedicated service to student success across four different institutions in three states. Her most recent role was Dean of People, Culture, and Society at American River College, where she co-led with faculty the development and implementation of Homebases, the centerpiece of the Guided Pathways framework. Additionally, Kathy has significantly contributed to dual enrollment efforts and co-chaired the professional development task force. Her experience includes positions as interim Dean of Counseling at American River College (ARC); Dean of Science, Math, and Engineering at Cosumnes River College; and Associate Dean of Business and Applied Arts at Madison Area Technical College in Wisconsin. Kathy’s career in academia began with teaching at Palo Alto College in San Antonio, Texas, an experience she credits with igniting her passion for community colleges. Her extensive leadership roles at ARC also included Academic Senator, and Academic Senate President. Kathy holds a B.S. in Biology from Baylor University, an M.S. in Biology from The University of Texas at Arlington, and a Ph.D. in Science Education from The University of Texas at Austin.

Ms. Ariana Velasco was appointed as Vice President of Student Services in October 2024. Ariana first joined WCC in 2012 and has a diverse set of Student Services experience including program development, resource allocation, categorical support programming, and overseeing core services such as Admissions & Records and Outreach & Student Engagement. As a proud first-generation college student and Woodland resident, Ariana entered higher education with a mindset of advocating for students, championing for equity, and enriching the student experience and educational opportunities for our communities.

Korinda Ebenhack, Dean of Lake County Campus and Colusa Center

An accomplished higher education professional with 30 years of experience in student affairs across California, Oregon, and Washington state, Korinda Ebenhack has been selected as the Dean of Lake County Campus and Colusa Center. A graduate of Butte Community College, she earned her BA degree from Rice University and returned to the west coast to earn her MA from Chico State. She began her community college career as a counselor and instructor at Yuba Community College. Ebenhack has served as a senior executive for 22 years at Rogue Community College in Oregon, most recently serving as Vice President of Student Services where she led initiatives in retention strategies and streamlining the recruitment and admissions process for students. Her diverse career includes roles such as counselor, Athletic Director, ADA Compliance officer, Title IX Investigator, Club Advisor and Dean of Students.

Dr. Carrie Monlux, Dean of Agriculture, Business and STEM

Dr. Monlux has over 30 years of experience in education. Born and raised on her family’s farm north of Chico, she began her career as a high school agriculture instructor and FFA advisor at Chico High School, and later taught agriculture, horticulture, and ag science classes at Butte College, California State University, Chico, and Texas A&M University. Carrie’s leadership spans STEM education, CTE program development, noncredit innovation, distance education, and workforce preparation. She is committed to expanding access and strengthening pathways that prepare students for high-demand careers.

excerpts.line: Chancellor Pan’s Monthly Virtual “Open Door” Sessions
window: When asked what advice has stayed with her throughout her career, Ana shared: “Lead with kindness, but don’t be afraid to have difficult conversations. People may not always remember what you said, but they’ll always remember how you made them feel.”
With her passion for people, problem-solving, and finding innovative ways to support employees, Ana looks forward to continuing to make a positive impact across the District.
Chancellor Pan’s Monthly Virtual “Open Door” Sessions

To better accommodate busy schedules and connect with more members of our campus community, Chancellor Pan will continue to offer monthly virtual Chancellor’s Open Door sessions for the 2026-2027 academic year.
These informal gatherings provide faculty, staff, and students across the Yuba Community College District an opportunity to engage directly with the Chancellor in a relaxed, conversational setting.
Have a question, idea, or just want to say hello? Stop by virtually and join the conversation.
